turns.doctor_question: Hi, it's good to meet you. What brings you in today?
turns.patient_response: I’ve been getting really preoccupied with how I look. Since I started helping with the safety trainings, I keep noticing how wrinkled and uneven my hands look when I’m pointing things out. And in the newsletter photos, I think my face looks crooked, even though people tell me they don’t see it.

symptom_reasoning.S067: The patient reports being very preoccupied with perceived wrinkles and unevenness of their hands and a crooked appearance of their face that others do not see.

turns.doctor_question: Do you find yourself repeatedly checking your hands or face in mirrors or photos?
turns.patient_response: Yes. Before I teach a class or do a workshop, I’ll look in the bathroom mirror a few times. I put lotion on my hands and turn my face different ways to check it. Sometimes I ask a coworker if I look all right too. It can make me a little late, but I still get there.

symptom_reasoning.S068: The patient reports repeatedly checking her face in the bathroom mirror from different angles and seeking reassurance from a coworker about her appearance.

turns.doctor_question: Do you believe for certain that your face is actually crooked, even when other people tell you it looks normal?
turns.patient_response: I mean, when I see the photos, it really does look crooked to me. But other people keep saying they don’t see it, so... I guess I’m not completely certain.

symptom_reasoning.S067: The patient reports perceiving their face as crooked in photos despite others saying they do not see it, indicating an appearance-related preoccupation.

turns.doctor_question: Have you ever avoided a class, workshop, or being in a photo because you felt too worried about how your face or hands looked?
turns.patient_response: I haven’t skipped work or the trainings because of it. But I do take longer getting ready, and lately I’ve been trying to stay out of photos. I sometimes hesitate about social things I used to just go to without thinking so much.

symptom_reasoning.S068: The patient reports taking longer to get ready and actively trying to stay out of photos because of appearance-related worry.

turns.doctor_question: When you hesitate about social things, is it mainly because you’re worried people will notice something wrong with your face or hands?
turns.patient_response: Yes, mostly. I start thinking people might notice, so I hesitate before going to social things. It hasn’t kept me from working or volunteering, but I take longer getting ready for trainings, and I’ve been ducking out of photos more.

symptom_reasoning.S067: The patient confirms that worries people will notice something wrong with their appearance contribute to hesitation about social events and avoidance of photos.

turns.doctor_question: When you’re around other people, do you worry about being judged even when it has nothing to do with how your face or hands look?
turns.patient_response: I’m not sure I’ve noticed that otherwise. Mostly it’s about how I look.

turns.doctor_question: Aside from worries about how your face or hands look, do you have any other unwanted thoughts that lead you to do things over and over, like checking, counting, or washing?
turns.patient_response: No, I don’t think so. I haven’t noticed other thoughts that make me check or wash or count things over and over.

symptom_reasoning.S065: The patient denies noticing other unwanted thoughts that lead to repetitive behaviors.
symptom_reasoning.S066: The patient denies repetitive checking, washing, or counting behaviors driven by other thoughts.
